# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-361 round 4 @ `400718f`, TIER 1) | **GO-with-findings, BLOCKER CLOSED — and it widened the builder's own load-bearing census rather than checking it.** 24 real-server runs (12 states x 2 heads), each boot -> act at the wire -> interrupt -> boot on the SAME DATA_DIR, every 503 attributed to the server's own `[auth] DENY:` line. The census re-run over a WIDER frame than claimed — 678 tracked files PLUS all of `node_modules` (0 hits) PLUS the Docker build context (proving no shipped test helper can write the key) — with both writers driven at the wire and their stamps ASSERTED, all four computed-key `setSetting` sites checked and all three wholesale settings writers read individually. **It caught its OWN first probe design using an ungated route as the SUBJECT, so it could not fail**, and swapped to `/api/data-sources`. Two runs discarded and re-done because `restoreFromBackupsIfNeeded()` silently merged a tamper back — reported, not smoothed. Controls that flip BOTH ways (state I r3 503 -> r4 200; state C3 r3 200 -> r4 503). F-1 found a sentence MEASURED FALSE in two artefacts, and was scrupulous about what it would NOT charge to this round (PREVGEN pre-existing, both heads serve). F-2 named round 3's failure class one level down: a census correct when written and undefended by any test. | **1.0** | ~21 min. Frame limits named unprompted (`8eb94ce` a bulk import, so the age claim holds over recorded history only; it did not read Jira and said so). **That last gap was real: Wednesday's completion check found F-1's false sentence in a THIRD artefact, RD-361 comment 37266.** One housekeeping omission: it booted 24 servers and its housekeeping section never claims to have stopped them — `pane_close.sh` caught a listener dying with its pane (16 -> 15) after the verdict. Harmless; the line is already in the RD-148 brief. |
| Datasec/NexusAI S45 (RD-361 round 4 @ `400718f` + RD-148 round 2 @ `ea4d229`, both PASS to gate) | **It falsified Wednesday's own premise before building on it, and that is the whole round.** Told to test the inference first, it enumerated every byte of every file across the state space, found `authEnforced_updated_at` surviving deletion of the key, said a discriminator DOES exist and STOPPED — exactly as instructed. **Its own control nearly gave the opposite answer**: its first harness gave each state a fresh temp directory and manufactured two differences that read as findings; it caught that, re-ran with them preserved, and LED its mail with the near-miss. Hunted the thing that would kill its candidate (`git log -S` on the age caveat; read the one `delete …_updated_at` rather than counting it). Red-proofed PER CLAUSE. On RD-148: proved the fix by CONTRAST (round-1 code + the new fixture = 10 FAILED, same product code) rather than by assertion, drove a real browser with measured box geometry and colour, **hashed its own screenshots and quarantined two byte-identical ones with a `WHY.md`**, and caught a probe polluting its own request count. Wrote the L4 exclusion in its own words in four places. | **1.0** | One deviation, flagged not absorbed, and it was RIGHT: told to file two tickets, it filed one because its own search found RD-368 already covered L4 — the standing rule beating Wednesday's instruction, and the instruction was the defective half. Deduction none: F-1 and F-2 from the gate are a boundary sentence and a missing guard, both cheap, neither a defect in what it built. |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s148) | **#897 MERGED — develop `400517aaf`, the deploy blocker closed on
